subject: Multivariate multilevel Function-on-Scalar Regression using Rstan, help!

messages.author: 69692f19baac3e71
messages.subject: Multivariate multilevel Function-on-Scalar Regression using Rstan, help!
parts:
Hi all,

I am attempting to fit a normal multivariate, multilevel function-on-scalar regression model that has smooth functional responses, scalar covariates, and smooth functional effects. I am attempting to adopt the framework laid out in J. Goldsmith, T. Kitago (2016). Assessing Systematic Effects of Stroke on Motor Control using Hierarchical Function-on-Scalar Regression. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C, 65 215-236. 

When I run the model (I am using a m4.4xlarge EC2 instance with Rstudio, stan, etc), all I get is the following error message:

Error : std::bad_alloc
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

I have attached my .stan code and R data prep file. I am pretty new to Stan, so there may be a pretty fundamental issue I am missing. Moreover, I am interested in figuring out some general strategies for debugging my code.


Thanks!
Kyle Payne
Data Scientist, Nielsen Research
kylen...@gmail.com

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multivariate multilevel Function-on-Scalar Regression using Rstan, help!
parts:
Sorry for the delay. I'm always hoping other people
will jump in on some of these questions.

You're probably allocating too much memory somewhere.
Stan requires about 24 bytes per function evaluation
plus 8 bytes per argument. You have at least
D^2 * n^2 loops and some potentially large matrices.

If at all possible, simplifying the matrices to scalar
or smaller matrix operations is much much more efficient.
As is vectorizing wherever possible.

We don't recommend the priors you're using (diffuse inverse
gamma and hard interval constraints [I know Andrew, I owe you
a syntax checker to auto-warn users against these things]) on
statistical (and computational) grounds.

- Bob
